summary: Training cycle ownership is now nonblocking and OS-owned across threads/processes; diagnostic TTL cannot steal an active owner, foreign callers cannot release it, and an OS-released crash owner can be reclaimed without replaying a training attempt. A stable guard inode and uniquely-created atomic diagnostic receipt avoid shared temporary-file races. Legacy live/unknown ownership is preserved, not assumed stopped. Busy cycles publish only a separate training_daemon_status.json diagnostic and cannot race primary train_status.json; owner-cycle failures preserve the original training attempt. All4 original regressions fail before repair. 28 new repository cases and198 focused checks pass in both roots (D116.09s/C114.21s), no skips. 6113 cases collected; complete new-revision two-OS CI remains pending. No operator fit, model activation, provider request or trading was launched. This is source/QA concurrency acceptance, not financial profitability or full-strategy acceptance.

contracts: TTL is diagnostic only, not authority to steal an active OS lock
Acquiring process and original Thread object alone may release the owner
The stable .training.lock.guard file is never unlinked and does not alone indicate an active process
Process exit releases the OS lock; the diagnostic JSON is reclaimable only under a fresh OS lock
A live or inaccessible legacy PID remains busy regardless of elapsed TTL
Malformed or unsupported legacy lock receipts are preserved for diagnosis, not silently deleted
Busy-cycle state is separate from authoritative primary training status
Existing candidate/activation/financial acceptance contracts are unchanged

shutdown.qualification: Read-only census. QA is not operational bot/training/AutoResearch approval. SQL checked separately.

read_only_sql.query: SELECT closed, COUNT(*) AS positions FROM positions WHERE dry_run=0 AND entry_lane='pump_early_green_candle_sniper' GROUP BY closed

limits: Current full Windows/Linux CI is not yet acceptance for these changes
Synthetic temporary model fixtures are software QA, not operator training or profitability
The lock API protects the native daemon cycle, not every possible direct standalone model writer
No timeout or automatic termination of a legitimately long-running training owner is introduced
Corrupt legacy ownership requires diagnosis rather than fabricated recovery
All original ten remaining whole-goal requirements and no-LIVE boundaries remain in force
